_comment: Literature and manufacturer evidence per thiol-relevant strain. Paraphrased from Resources/research/2026-05-13_hoparoma-yeast-scale-audit/source.md and manufacturer disclosures. Source ids point to data/sources.json anchors. Only strains listed here get an individual page.

cosmic_punch.summary: A British ale strain (Omega British V lineage) with its native IRC7 β-lyase promoter activated, so it releases bound hop thiols far more than its parent.

evidence.text: Omega describes Cosmic Punch as a thiol-releasing strain built on its British V ale yeast; trade coverage reports free-thiol levels around ten times the sensory threshold in test beers.
It is the reference point Omega uses for its later patB strains: Helio Gazer is marketed as producing many times more thiols than Cosmic Punch.

cosmic_punch.practical: Ferments like a soft British ale strain. Feed it precursors: mash or whirlpool hops rich in bound 3MH, and Phantasm if you use it. Keep oxygen away after fermentation, because the thiols it releases oxidise quickly.
cosmic_punch.gmo_note: Engineered (IRC7 promoter change). Check local labelling rules before selling beer made with it.

star_party.summary: A Chico-type (West Coast) ale strain carrying a patB β-lyase, giving thiol release on a clean, neutral fermentation base.

evidence.text: Omega positions Star Party as its clean-base thiol strain; the parent Chico strain has very low native β-lyase activity, so the patB enzyme is what does the work.

star_party.practical: Choose it when you want West Coast clarity and attenuation with a tropical lift, rather than a soft hazy profile.

thiol_libre.summary: A conventionally bred (non-GMO) strain selected for very high native β-lyase activity.

evidence.text: Escarpment Labs classifies Thiol Libre as very high for thiol biotransformation and describes it as bred, not genetically modified; a 2023 update removed the phenolic character of the early release.

thiol_libre.practical: The usual homebrew-friendly route to strong thiol release without an engineered strain. Confirm you have the current, non-phenolic version.

berkeley_tropics.summary: A London-type ale strain carrying a protein-engineered carbon-sulfur lyase designed to release tropical thiols selectively while limiting off-flavours.

evidence.text: Berkeley Yeast discloses that Tropics uses an engineered lyase chosen for selectivity toward the tropical thiols, on a London ale parent.

berkeley_tropics.practical: Sold in professional pitch sizes; homebrewers rarely see it. Behaves like a soft London ale strain otherwise.

wlp077_tropicale.summary: A non-GMO blend of two conventional strains that White Labs found to have high β-lyase activity, offered as a homebrew-friendly alternative to engineered thiol yeasts.

evidence.text: White Labs screened its library for β-lyase activity and blended WLP037 Yorkshire Square with WLP830 German Lager; in a split-batch trial against WLP001, gas chromatography found 3MHA above its sensory threshold only in the WLP077 beer.

wlp077_tropicale.practical: Attenuation around 75 to 82 percent with low flocculation, so expect some haze. A good first thiol yeast for anyone who wants to avoid engineered strains.

helio_gazer.summary: The same British V parent as Cosmic Punch, but carrying a patB β-lyase, which Omega reports as far more active and more specific than the native IRC7 enzyme.

evidence.text: Omega markets Helio Gazer as boosting free thiols to around two hundred times the sensory threshold and as producing many times more thiols than Cosmic Punch; those are concentration claims in finished beer, not conversion yields.

helio_gazer.practical: Easy to overshoot. Treat precursor-rich hops and Phantasm as a dial, not a default, and manage oxygen strictly.

lalbrew_pomona.summary: A hybrid IPA strain developed by Lallemand with Escarpment Labs, characterised for both terpene and thiol biotransformation.

evidence.text: Lallemand describes Pomona as having excellent potential for terpene biotransformation and for thiol biotransformation; brewer comparisons report more passionfruit and guava character than Verdant IPA in side-by-side batches.

lalbrew_pomona.practical: Dry, widely available, and forgiving. A medium-activity strain rather than a thiol specialist, so pair it with precursor-rich hops if tropical is the goal.

saflager_sh45.summary: A dry lager strain (Saccharomyces pastorianus) that Fermentis selected for its ability to release and esterify hop thiols, launched in late 2025.

evidence.text: Fermentis states that SH-45 can release and esterify thiols, so beers made with it may show more fruitiness and stronger citrus and tropical notes when hopped with thiol-rich varieties.
Lager yeast releasing thiols from both hop and malt precursors during fermentation has been demonstrated in peer-reviewed work, which is the mechanism this strain is selected for.

saflager_sh45.practical: A route to thiol character in hoppy lagers and cold IPA without an ale strain. Cold fermentation slows the enzyme, so give it precursor-rich hops in the whirlpool and time. Independent measurements are still scarce; treat the high rating as the manufacturer's positioning until third-party data appears.

whitelabs_wlp830.summary: A classic German lager strain that White Labs identified as having unusually high β-lyase potential in its library screen.

evidence.text: White Labs reports that WLP830 German Lager showed relatively high potential β-lyase activity, which is why it became one half of the WLP077 Tropicale blend.

whitelabs_wlp830.practical: Useful for cold IPA and hoppy lagers where you want thiol lift without ale esters. Cold fermentation slows enzyme activity, so the effect is gentler than in an ale.
